summary: A clean, current Forbes 2026 top 10 that a news-following player nearly clears (casual found 9), so it is too easy for today's daily bar. Famous near misses cost lives fast, and several show stale or no figures.
reasons: Casual found 9 of 10 in 15 guesses (lives lost on Gates, Ambani, Ballmer, Bloomberg); Page, Brin, Ellison and Arnault fall easily for anyone who follows the news, and only Ortega is a real stretch. Above the 6 to 8 bar.
Fan also found 9 but spent all 5 lives on real near misses (Ballmer, Gates, Dell, Jim and Rob Walton) before reaching Ortega.
Top 10, names and all 10 fun facts are clean; the reveal is the weak spot: Dell shows "#9 in 2000 ($19.1 billion)", Adani and Bettencourt Meyers show nothing.
fixes: No figure on a miss for Gautam Adani and Françoise Bettencourt Meyers (both added via `more`). Dated figures exist: List of Indians by net worth, table 0 (Adani $84 billion, #2 in India; caption undated) and List of French billionaires by net worth, table 0, 2023 Forbes list (Bettencourt Meyers $80.5 billion, #2 in France).

Stale reveals mislead: Michael Dell "#9 in 2000 ($19.1 billion)", Jim/Alice/S. Robson Walton "#8/#9/#10 in 2020 (about $54 billion)", Charles Koch "#8 in 2018 ($60 billion)". List of Americans by net worth, table 0 (US top 25 as of December 2025) has newer figures: Ballmer $153B (#7 US), Dell $129B (#10), Rob Walton $118B (#11), Jim Walton $115B (#12), Bloomberg $109B (#13), Gates $107B (#14), Alice Walton $106B (#15), Charles Koch $73.8B (#17). Show the newest dated figure per person, labelled as a US rank, e.g. "Michael Dell: $129 billion, #10 in the US (Dec 2025)". (Bloomberg Billionaires Index, table 1, has Dell #6 at $223 billion as of July 13, 2026, but that is a different index from the prompt's Forbes list.)

World ranks 11+ cannot come from Wikipedia: The World's Billionaires has only top-10 tables per year (List of richest people in the world redirects to it) and the Bloomberg Billionaires Index page lists only a top 10. The REBUILD_QUEUE item asking for ranks 11-25 should become dated figures from the country tables above.

Walton family: "the walton family" costs a life and shows "#2 in 1998 ($48.0 billion)", while "waltons" is not recognized (free). Skip the family rows like the deceased (the prompt is about people; Jim, Alice and Rob stay as costly near misses with current figures), or alias "Waltons" and give the family a current figure.
